relevant_issues.body:
Jiang et al. (2018), DOI [10.1080/01490451.2017.1377320](https://doi.org/10.1080/01490451.2017.1377320), has complete article-text access through a public author-upload PDF. Original Figures 1–8 remain unavailable for visual inspection after bounded legitimate acquisition attempts. No record or history was admitted.

The round40 assessment is prepared at `research/sources/round40-samarium-phosphate/20261012T005055Z-source-deferral.md` with a paired JSON acquisition log. It will be published with the current curation PR.

Acceptance work:

- Obtain and inspect original microscopy, diffraction and EXAFS graphics, including control/axis/biomass details and Figure 7 phase indexing; inventory relevant supplements.
- Retain or resolve the reported 0.1 versus 0.01 M NaCl, 23±2 versus 25±1 °C, P. fluorescens 0.3 versus 0.6 dry g/L, and 92 versus 96 h differences.
- Assess source-assigned monazite(Sm) against SAED, the hydrated SmPO4 EXAFS standard and preparation/mixture limits; formula or EDS alone does not establish mineral identity.
- Preserve the historical B. subtilis IAM 1069 label while grounding its current JCM 20035 B. spizizenii mapping. Resolve strain/biomass uncertainty without inferring culture authentication or transferring earlier yeast viability assays.
- Curate only supported claims, with canonical history, independent review and corpus gates. Solution depletion does not establish isolated recovery or industrial deployment.

This remains a source-verification task, separate from the Jiang2010 cerium study in #130. Complete-text recovery and documented deferral do not resolve the missing original graphics.

relevant_issues.body:
Jiang et al. (2010), [DOI 10.1016/j.chemgeo.2010.07.010](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.chemgeo.2010.07.010), reports yeast-associated cerium-phosphate particles. Available metadata/outreach describe a monazite-like structure, rather than establishing rhabdophane. The complete 2010 methods and original phase evidence remain unavailable through the checked legitimate routes; the Elsevier XML response contains core metadata only.

A later coauthor paper, [Ochiai and Utsunomiya (2017), DOI 10.3390/min7050084](https://doi.org/10.3390/min7050084), qualifies earlier identification because diffuse diffraction and amorphous material prevented full particle identification. This is not a formal correction or proof of a different mineral species. No record or CREATE history was admitted from the abstract.

Complete this evidence review:

- Acquire the complete 2010 article or legitimate author manuscript, original diffraction/microscopy, tables and relevant supplements. Reconcile the original assignment with the 2017 qualification.
- Verify mineral identity, hydration, preparation/beam effects, strain and biomass state, phosphorus carryover, matched controls, concentrations, timepoints and measured denominators.
- Keep mineral species, elemental cerium and separate experiments distinct. Do not infer a named mineral or inherited criticality from nominal CePO4 or elemental spectra.
- Curate only defensible claims in the correct material owner after full-source review, canonical history and exact-hash independent scientific review; otherwise preserve the source-only deferral.

This tracks unresolved source acquisition and identification, not a corrective finding against the current corpus. Bounded acquisition attempts and the explicit deferral protect accepted records but do not resolve the evidence gap.

source_assessments.identity: Bamforth et al. (2024), Chemical Geology 666:122307; Crossref verifies title/authors and PII S0009254124003875. Main obtained from Adelaide institutional repository; supplementary workbook obtained from Elsevier CDN.
source_assessments.inspected: Complete 17-page original read; visual pages 3-15 cover all experimental Figures 2-10, Tables 1-3, methods and discussion; Figure 1 is an introductory structural model. Supplement EPMA (Analysis) and EPMA (Data) worksheet cells inspected, standards/limits and representative RDP_Ce rows checked. Oxygen is calculated stoichiometrically, not directly measured water.
source_assessments.adopted: Synthetic Ce-rich rhabdophane prepared from Durango fluorapatite, powder-diffraction phase identification; 180 C/8 h, nominal pH1, 1 M H3PO4 98.6% versus 0.1 M HCl 6.4% fitted relative crystalline replacement; microscopy supports interpreted dissolution-precipitation.
limitations: Not recovery yield; no biotic treatment, deployment, exact hydration or universal crystal symmetry.
Preparative 96-hour run repeated eleven times, not eleven replicates of each hydrothermal condition; nine homogenized portions used for nine fluids.
Section 2.1.2 loading 20 ± 0.1 mg conflicts with Table 1 values 20.9–21.1 mg.
Section 3.1 pH3 <5% statement conflicts with Figure 3 values 4.4, 4.7, 6.4%; preserve without correction or kinetic extrapolation.
Section 3.1 calls pH1 phosphate runs entire replacement, but numerical fractions 98.6/98.5% are near-complete, not 100%.
Figure 10 and section 4.3.2 show porosity-related overlapping microprobe totals; cannot identify an unrelated Ce phosphate using elemental composition alone.
Equation 2 printed water coefficient x versus three hydrated products appears unbalanced; no balanced equation is imported.
Supplement sample labels repeat and include section headings; physical worksheet rows are not independent-specimen counts. No import or WT%-to-mg/kg conversion.

source_assessments.adopted: La-specific 200 mg, 1100 C/6h air transformation and starting/product PXRD; La 0.804 and Ce 0.732 total-water coefficients are sample-specific TGA estimates including adsorbed and structural water.
limitations: Samples same series as Mesbah2017; not independent replication.
C2 fitted starting model based on prior structure, not universal resolution of rhabdophane symmetry.

Abstract says water decreases with increasing radius while Table2 data go the other way; generalized trend not adopted. Pages4–5 give conflicting directions for temperature trends, so no universal exact transition threshold.
Table5 Ce Gibbs reaction value -6.2 ±14.4 kJ/mol spans zero; no blanket all-conditions equilibrium stability claim adopted.
Ce oxidation in calorimetric solvent is not an observed Ce(IV) starting phosphate; no redox claim.
No thermal reversibility or commercial/biological test.

source_assessments.inspected: Complete 24-page original acquired from RRUFF; text read and all Figures1–10/Tables1–6 and relevant methods/discussion visually inspected. Main-study claim pages1280–1284, Table4p1290, Fig7p1291 and Fig10p1295.
source_assessments.adopted: Natural La-dominant members in compositionally zoned mixed rhabdophane-group grains, Velence Hills, supported by microprobe and Raman; only qualified natural context.
limitations: Natural 5–25 micrometre grains have Ca/Th/U/Fe and mixed end-member contributions; not pure end-member samples. Some group-II grains are Nd-dominant despite general La enrichment.
Formula normalization and Raman do not individually quantify hydration of every grain; low oxide totals alone cannot identify phase.
No diffraction refinement or controlled microbial mechanism in this natural study; geological origin inferred from assemblage.
Original p1296 Fe formula statement corrected by 2019 erratum; follow correction.
No separate supplement is cited in inspected original; no exhaustive publisher supplement-absence claim.
